Subject: ACME integration: post-call recap & next steps (SDK / auth / prompts)

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary use case: customer support agent augmentation (long docs + product KB + API results) with a reranker + structured tool calls for actions (create ticket, fetch account).
- Key constraints: PII/sensitive data, on-prem/VPC storage for embeddings preferred, strict audit and versioning requirements for prompts and system prompts.
- Current infra: mostly AWS, security team owns KMS and SSO.

Technical areas we touched and recommended approaches:
1) SDK setup & auth
- Options: API key + mTLS for hosted; service account with IAM + short-lived tokens for Dedicated/Private.
- For ACME security posture we recommend service-account tokens + KMS-wrapped keys (we can support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments).

2) Routing & model variants
- Smart routing: latency-sensitive (small model) vs high-quality (large model) lanes.
- Fallbacks: quantized variant if capacity constrained; automatic region routing.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- Use Redwood's structured output schema (JSON schema + tool registry) so downstream systems can parse reliably.
- Tool calling supported via explicit function signatures (name + args schema).

4) Embeddings & reranker
- Options: store embeddings in your VPC (recommended) or encrypted at rest in our storage.
- Reranker: two-stage approach (BM25 / ANN retrieval -> neural reranker using candidate embeddings).

5) Prompt templates & system prompt governance
- Version prompts in a Git-backed prompt store, tag releases, and tie prompts to eval suites.
- Prompt injection mitigations: input sanitization, instruction-scoped system prompt boundaries, and red-team tests for adversarial inputs.
- Red teaming: periodic adversarial prompt runs + automated regression alerts on quality metrics.

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (checklist for SDK/auth/network)
- prototype-architecture.drawio (diagram we sketched)

Next steps (proposed):
- Tech deep dive: 60m with Dylan to walk SDK+tooling next week (possible times: Tue/Wed 10-12 PT)
- Security call: 30m with Rishi to go through SOC2, KMS options, data flow (Thursday preferred)
- Share a short prompt-governance proposal and red-team checklist before the security call

Can you confirm times that work and if we should include any other folks (security, platform)?

Best,
Marissa

Samir — great questions, answered inline below. Quoting your points for clarity.

On Mon, 13 Jul 2026 at 09:22 AM Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com> wrote:
> - Embeddings: when you say "store embeddings in our VPC" are you referring to a managed customer-owned S3 bucket + VPC endpoint, or do you expect an on-prem vector DB? Our security team is concerned about cold-starts and the need to rotate encryption keys.

Short answer: both are supported. More detail: 
- Managed customer-owned S3 + VPC endpoint: recommended for fast integration. Embeddings are encrypted with your KMS; Redwood's inference nodes use ephemeral credentials to access via VPC endpoints. Key rotation is supported via your KMS policies.
- On-prem / customer-hosted vector DB: supported for Private deployments; we provide connectors for Milvus/Pinecone/Matrix and can run the reranker inside your environment so raw PII never leaves your VPC.

> - Reranker: does the neural reranker require sending raw PII to Redwood inference, or can it run entirely within our VPC?

You can run the reranker inside your VPC for Private deployments (recommended). For Hosted/Dedicated, we offer encryption-in-transit and at-rest; but if ACME policy forbids external inference on PII, we should plan for a Private deployment and run the neural reranker in your environment.

Attachments I've dropped: SOC2 report + a short SLA/comms table so Procurement has something to review.

Proposed next steps (updated):
- Tech deep dive (Dylan): 60m to confirm SDK auth flow, VPC setup, and structured output schemas
- Security deep dive (Rishi): 30m to walk ACME security team through KMS, key rotation, and red-team results

If that makes sense I'll send calendar invites for Tue/Wed slots and a one-pager on prompt governance ahead of the security call.

Thanks,
Marissa

Samir, Olivia —
Short tech note ahead of the deep dive. I'll walk through these live but wanted to put a few implementation notes here.

1) SDK & auth flow (example):
- Recommended: service account + short-lived JWT tied to customer KMS. Flow:
  1. ACME backend signs a JWT for the Redwood service account
  2. Redwood validates signature + issues short-lived inference token (1-5m)
  3. Inference requests carry the short-lived token; logs include token-id for audit

2) Structured output / tool calling example (pseudo):
- Request payload: {
  "input": "Summarize user issue and suggest action",
  "tools": ["create_ticket", "fetch_account"],
  "schema": "https://redwood-inference.com/schemas/support-action-v1.json"
}
- Tool registry entries include: name, args-schema, required-roles. The runtime validates model output against the schema before executing.

3) Embeddings / reranker
- For Private: reranker runs adjacent to the vector DB; only scores are returned to Redwood telemetry (aggregated).
- For Hosted: we recommend pseudonymization at ingestion and strict ACLs on the embedding store.

4) Prompt templates & governance (proposal):
- Git-backed prompt repo (repo-per-product). Each prompt gets a semantic version and a metadata header: created_by, created_at, eval_id, tags.
- Release process: tag -> CI runs evals and red-team tests -> approval -> deploy to runtime with immutable prompt-hash tied to model execution.
- Runtime: allow per-tenant overrides but enforce "system prompt" locked path for critical safety guards.

Example prompt header (simple):
# Prompt: support-assistant/summary-v1
# Version: 0.2.1
# Eval: eval-support-summary-20260701
# Notes: enforces ticket format, strips agent instructions from user-provided text

Questions to confirm on the call:
- Does ACME want prompts stored in your Git (we can mirror) or in our managed prompt store?
- Any compliance constraints around prompt history retention?

I'll bring a short slide with code snippets and the schema for structured output.

Thanks,
Dylan
